The “Could Mom Qualify for Medicaid?” Checklist

What to gather, write down and ask before you apply.

Download PDF

Mom needs care now, your family is paying for it, and somebody has said the word “Medicaid.” Before anyone looks at where she stands, make sure you have these in hand. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something still to find or ask, not a sign of where Mom stands.

Gather

Write down

Ask

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you gather, write down and ask. It doesn't say whether Mom may qualify, what any item means for her, or what to do about it, and a page full of checks isn't an answer either way. Medicaid rules vary by state, and nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice. Those questions go to your Medicaid planner or the appropriate licensed professional, and to the next step below.

Ready for the next step?

You know what to gather, what to write down and who to ask. The planning interview takes it from there: it asks about your family's situation, one question at a time, and gives you a free planning report you can bring to any conversation about paying for Mom's care.

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 or 2 follow what the Administration for Community Living and Medicaid.gov say a state looks at or may ask an applicant to document. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
